title: Kärnan
visualBrief: Helsingborg’s brick keep with its asymmetric octagonal stair turret, eight merlons per main elevation, recessed windows and putlog holes, sandstone belt, raised timber entrance, projecting northwest privy shaft, open roof terrace and low collar-wall remnants. Shared metric materials and original continuous brick weathering.

nativeAxes.front: Native -X faces southwest toward the city and sea; native -Z is the northwest privy elevation, +Z southeast.
nativeAxes.origin: Native-X faces southwest toward the city/sea; native-Z is the northwest privy side; native+Z southeast. Exact-Q1779457 way236992894 contains the asymmetric stair-turret projection. Hikuin19 article p43 explicitly names southwest principal facade/stair turret and northwest privy; inspected Fig2 plan and current2015/2025 exterior photos agree. Heading0.909308291221rad follows the mapped long edge, not a surveyed azimuth;±3degree map/photo estimate.

scaleBasis: Mapped main plan is about15.8×16.3 m, compared with the city’s approximately15 m description. Main crenellations reach the mapped34.5 m. Current photographs establish the taller turret and individual facade layouts; turret38.5 m and5.8 m entrance are provisional proportional reconstruction. The1893 section predates restoration, and operator floor labels are not substituted for surveyed exterior datums.

geographicProposal.evidence: Exact-QID OSM main footprint, including the offset stair turret, supplies anchor and axis. Hikuin19, printed p43 explicitly locates the stair turret on the southwest face and the privy projection on the northwest. Native -X is southwest and -Z northwest under the recorded heading; native +Z is southeast. The source preserves that signed frame.
geographicProposal.limitations: The main footprint and signed facade orientation are map/publication based. Ground levels, the reconstructed collar wall and timber stair need detailed site terrain and survey confirmation.

Static restored exterior: main34.5m battlements and approximately15m plan are city/preservation documented;38.5m turret,44.08m mast,5.8m threshold and minor openings are photographic proportions. Original detailed source is preserved. Current collar-wall remnants and timber approach are approximate plan/photo reconstructions, not surveyed ruins or terrain. Shared brick provides canonical repeating joints with original weathering in the detailed source; no scan or copied individual brick repair. Browser skyline uses facade marks, district omits subpixel putlog holes, street uses original flat dark marks, close-up retains physical putlog/window recesses. Small roof paving joints are averaged into an intact floor. Hidden interiors, archaeological predecessor, distant Terrace Stairs, landscape and temporary visitor equipment are excluded. Host must fit terrain contact locally; footprint replacement is disabled.
